page.layout: One printed page, single column. Running head at top, page number at top left. Lines 23–29 form a numbered list with German glosses. Two paragraphs follow, then a rule, a division heading with a subheading, and two more paragraphs. No margin notes, no catchword.

main_text.l: 23. Aut congregandi: ut, simul, zu gleich. Una, mit einander Pariter, zu gleich. Collectim, jempt ich.
24. Aut admirandi: ut, papæ, bthü e Gott. Hui, boz. Vah, wanne Proh, hüff Gott.
25. Aut cominandi: ut, Væ, væ, weh/weh.
26. Aut dolendi: ut, Hei, Ah, ey/ ey/ jo einer seuff-zet. Heu, ach[?].
27. Aut indignandi: ut, Hem, daß dich boz. Proh, ach/ ach Vah, pfau[?] ich an.
28. Aut exclamandi: ut, O, setter mordio.
29. Aut exultandi: ut, Evax, jauch hoschaho.
main_text.p: Authorü lectio plures suppeditabit species, quas, cum in infinitum pateant, nihil attinet hic recenseri, inquit Dominus Philippus Melanchthon.

Nonnulla Adverbia comparantur: ut, fortiter, fortius, fortissime. Celeriter, celerius, celerrime. Parum, minus, minime. Saepe, saepius, saepissime. Nuper, nuperrime. Magis, maxime. Satis, quàg/ satius, beß/ ser. Virg. Nonne fuit satius, id est, melius.
main_text.head: DE CONIUNCTIONE.
Quid est Conjunctio?
main_text.p: CONjunctio est vox sine numero, quae superiori sententiæ aut parti subinde aliam annectit. Conjunctio est Sextuplex: Copulativa, qua tam sensus, quam voces copulantur: Et, Que, vnd/ Quoq, auch. Ac, atq, vnd. Etiam, darzu. Simul, sampt. Cum, nicht allein. Tum, sondern auch.
Aut conditionalis, qua cum conditione sententia aut pars annectitur: ut, Cum, wenn. Dum, dieweil. Donec, so lange. Quatenus, so fern. Si, wann. Sin, wann aber. Nisi, wo nicht.

page.notes: Long s is printed as plain s throughout. "sine" appears as "fine" in the scan and is read as sine. Doubtful readings are marked [?]: "ach" in line 26, and the second word of line 27. The German glosses are black letter and are marked <bl>. The reading of "Virg." before "Nonne" is uncertain; it may be a citation. The rule above the heading is decorative and not transcribed. "Vnd" and similar forms are printed with u for v and are left as printed in the glosses.
